title: Ab Initio Investigation of Pressure Effects in the Spin-Liquid Candidate Y-Kapellasite
authors: Federico Abbruciati, Aleksandar Razpopov, Joao Elias F. S. Rodrigues, Gaston Garbarino, Matthieu Le Tacon, Roser Valenti, Pascal Puphal, Björn Wehinger
abstract: Motivated by recent experiments showing pressure-induced suppression of magnetic order and the emergence of a dynamical ground state in the anisotropic kagome antiferromagnet Y-kapellasite Y3Cu9(OH)19Cl8, we perform ab initio density functional theory (DFT)calculations to investigate the evolution of magnetic exchange interactions under hydrostatic pressure. We show that pressure efficiently tunes the magnetic Hamiltonian by altering the CuOCu bond geometry, thereby driving the system towards a spin-liquid regime. This evolution is governed by a nonlinear dependence of the dominant exchange coupling on the CuOCu bond angle. We further examine the influence of hydrogen positions and find that both the OH bond length and the hydrogen out-of-plane angle strongly affect the magnetic interactions. Our results provide a microscopic explanation for the experimentally observed pressure-induced enhancement of frustration and highlight the key role of hydrogen geometry.
summary: This work uses DFT calculations to microscopically explain how applying hydrostatic pressure tunes the magnetic interactions in Y-kapellasite, driving it toward a spin-liquid state. The study emphasizes that structural details, particularly Cu–O–Cu bond angles and hydrogen geometry, are the dominant physical controls governing this quantum phase transition.
main_problem: The study investigates how hydrostatic pressure drives the magnetic exchange interactions in Y-kapellasite, a spin-liquid candidate, towards a quantum spin-liquid regime.
main_result: Pressure efficiently tunes the magnetic Hamiltonian by altering the Cu–O–Cu bond geometry, confirming that hydrogen positioning and bond angles are crucial microscopic controls for frustration enhancement.
method: Ab initio Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were employed using Total Energy Mapping Analysis (TEMA) to calculate isotropic magnetic exchange couplings ($J', J_9, J$) under varying pressures and structural perturbations.
model_or_system: The system is the anisotropic kagome antiferromagnet Y-kapellasite. The magnetic behavior is modeled by an effective Heisenberg Hamiltonian involving three primary exchange couplings ($J'$, $J_9$, $J$).
key_observables: Magnetic exchange couplings ($J', J_9, J$), their pressure dependence, and the ratios of these couplings ($ rac{J'}{J_9}$, $ rac{J}{J_9}$) relative to a theoretical phase diagram.
important_parameters: Hydrostatic pressure (up to 7.9 GPa), Cu–O–Cu bond angle, O–H bond length, and hydrogen out-of-plane angle ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily focuses on the first three nearest-neighbor exchange parameters; certain calculations assume a constant value for the Hubbard U parameter calibrated to ambient $\theta_{CW}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the pressure evolution of coupling ratios onto a phase diagram, and other figures map the dependence of couplings on structural parameters like bond angles and hydrogen positions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of external tuning parameters (pressure, structure) on the magnetic Hamiltonian derived from DFT calculations, mapping the resulting state onto established theoretical phase diagrams for kagome magnets.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state magnetism, the methodology—using first principles to map structural changes into effective low-energy Hamiltonians and predicting quantum ground states (spin liquids)—is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated quantum materials.
